pairs.difference: A (chip): lit straight from above and the front. The board's top face is evenly bright from edge to edge. The die's left and right bevels look almost the same, and there is only a thin soft cast shadow on the lower right. Light bias is 0.177, below the real range. B (book): a clear key from the upper left. The page block and right spine edge fall into darker shadow, and a long cast shadow lies on the wood to the left and below.
pairs.fix: Light the chip from the upper left with one strong key. Make the right and bottom edges of the board and the die's right bevel clearly darker. Add a darker cast shadow on the table falling down and to the right, darkest where the board touches the table.

pairs.difference: B (sneakers): both shoes are lit almost evenly from the front. The left and right shoes have the same brightness and there is no side that turns away into shadow. The midsoles have bright white tops everywhere. Light bias is 0.019, far below real. A (helmet): a key from the upper left. The right half of the shell and the visor's right edge turn dark, with a soft cast shadow to the lower left.
pairs.fix: Light the sneakers from one side, upper left. Make the right side of each shoe and the inner faces of the collars clearly darker. Let the far shoe sit partly in the near shoe's shadow, and darken the floor under the toes and heels.

pairs.difference: B (locker): the door face and body front are lit flat and evenly. The light falls off only gently toward the right edge, the plastic-like rounded edges have the same soft sheen all round, and the shading has a warm pink cast. A (flask): a directional key from the left with a defined cast shadow on the right side of the counter. The glass has low contrast in the lens, but that looks like a transparency effect, not flat lighting.
pairs.fix: Light the locker from the left. Put the open door's inner face and the cabinet's right side into a deeper shadow, and darken the inside of the compartment toward the back. Add a firmer contact shadow under the feet on the floorboards.

pairs.difference: B (UFO): the saucer rim and dome are lit almost evenly all the way round. The dome has no dark side, the underside barely darkens, and the shading range of 0.525 is at the bottom of the real range. A (plane): a clear top-left key. The fuselage belly, the engine undersides and the far wing are distinctly darker, so the light turns into shadow across each cylinder.
pairs.fix: Light the saucer from the upper left. Make the underside of the rim and the right half of the dome clearly darker, and leave one small bright highlight on the upper-left of the dome. Make the lights along the rim go darker toward the right.

pairs.difference: A (bike on car): the frame and wheels are lit flat. The scene has a warm low sun, but the bike tubes show almost no light-to-shadow turn, and the car's rear is uniformly mid-dark. Shading range is 0.549, below real. B (rover): a hard key from the left with crisp, dark cast shadows on the regolith and a clear lit and shadow side on the fenders. That is strong, but it reads as a deliberate single light.
pairs.fix: Light the bike with the low sun from the left side. Make the right side of each tube and the far wheel noticeably darker, and add a thin warm rim of light along the top edges of the frame and saddle. Let the bike cast a shadow onto the car's tailgate.

pairs.difference: B (balloons): each balloon has a soft highlight at the upper left and a gentle darkening at the lower right. The shadow side stays shallow, the balloons hardly shadow each other, and form contrast is 0.363, near the low end. A (rocket): a strong left key. The right side of the body and the right fin go clearly darker, and the shading turns quickly across the cylinder. Light bias is 0.701.
pairs.fix: Make the lower-right side of each balloon go into a deeper shadow. Where balloons overlap, put a darker shadow on the one behind. Keep one small sharp highlight on the upper left of each.

pairs.difference: B (rose arch): lit frontally. The leaves and roses on the left and right pillars are equally bright, there is no side of the arch that turns away, and there is only a faint soft shadow on the floor. The lens shows a bright central glow behind the arch. Light bias is 0.14, below real. A (column): a strong warm key from the upper left. The volutes, the flutes and the right side of the shaft fall into deep shadow, with a cast shadow on the plinth.
pairs.fix: Light the arch from the upper left. Make the right pillar and the inner face of the arch noticeably darker than the left, and let the leaves shadow one another more deeply. Add darker contact shadows where the pillars meet the floor.

pairs.difference: A (vault door): lit head-on. The ring, the bolts and the wheel are evenly bright all round, the hinges cast only faint shadows, and there is no lit side and shadow side across the circular frame. Light bias is 0.141, below real. B (gate): directional light. The brick pillars have a lit front and a darker side face, and the gate and pillars cast shadows on the paving.
pairs.fix: Light the vault door from the upper left. Make the lower-right part of the metal ring and the right side of each bolt darker, and have the hinges cast clear dark shadows onto the wall to the right. Make the inside of the door recess darker.

pairs.difference: A (control panel): the front, top and side faces are close in value. The light falls off gently, the side face is only slightly darker, and the console has a weak contact shadow on the counter. Light bias is 0.235, near the low end. B (claw machine): the right side of the cabinet is clearly darker, the interior is lit by a practical lamp, and the lit and shadow sides separate clearly.
pairs.fix: Light the console from the upper left. Make the right side face clearly darker than the front, and darken the inside of the screen bezel. Have the levers and the button cast small shadows down and to the right, and add a darker contact shadow under the base.

pairs.difference: B (target booth): the target and bear are lit from the front by the row of bulbs. The target face is evenly bright, the bear's sides are equally lit, and the only shadow is a soft one behind the easel. A (chess table): a very strong sun key with hard, dark cast shadows on the grass and a clearly darker side face on the table. Light bias is 0.971, above range, but it is consistent with daylight.
pairs.fix: Let the bulbs light from the top. Make the lower half of the target and the bear's legs darker, and put a darker shadow on the right side of the bear. Have the target and easel cast a clear shadow onto the back wall and shelf.

pairs.difference: A (fan): window light from the left, but the grille and blades are fairly evenly lit, and the hub has only a mild shading turn. Light bias is 0.247. B (dish): a clear key, a defined dark cast shadow on the roof to the right, and a darker underside of the bowl. There is only weak evidence either way.
pairs.fix: Make the window light on the fan stronger from the left. Darken the right half of the grille and the hub's right side, and cast the shadow of the grille onto the wall behind.

pairs.difference: B (satellite): the lens shows a bright halo centered behind the satellite and is lit from behind. The foil cube carries scattered small hot spots, while its faces and the panels sit at similar mid values. Light bias is 0.906, above real. A (medal box): a clean upper-left key. The right outer wall of the box and the inner lid go darker, and the coin has a lit top-left and a shadowed lower-right.
pairs.fix: Remove the glow behind the satellite. Light it from the upper left: the top face of the cube is brightest, the left face is mid and the right face is dark. Make the solar panels darker on their far halves, and keep the foil highlights to a few broad soft sheens instead of many small sparkles.

pattern: Generated cards are lit from the front and evenly. Both sides of the hero have nearly the same brightness, the shadow side stays shallow, and cast and contact shadows are faint (very low light_bias_strength). Some put a bright halo behind the subject instead of a single side key, sometimes with scattered small hot spots. Real cards commit to one upper-left key, with a clearly darker right or under side and defined shadows on the ground.
